hbm.channels.justification: HBM channel count.  The two design points state different HBM provisioning: the ROM point carries 5 HBM3E stacks on each of 4 devices (area_fractions.hbm_phy 0.06135 of 815 mm2 at 10 mm2 per stack) serving KV alone at points[ROM].kv_transfer_bytes_per_step / component_times_s.kv_read = 1.8e13 B/s, while the GPU point carries 2 B200 packages of 8 stacks serving weights AND KV from one pool at points[GPU].peak_weight_read_bytes_s = 1.44e13 B/s.  Both resolve to the SAME hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel; only the channel count differs, which is exactly what the design points say differs.

rom.arrays.justification: ROM array count.  The ROM design point stores its weights in ROM and the GPU design point has no ROM at all; the HBM machine carries a single inert array because the cost-table schema requires the full parameter set, and no MEMORY_OBJECT in the HBM deployment is stamped StorageClass.ROM, so it is never read.

rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array.justification: Per-array ROM read rate.  Derived on the ROM machine from points[ROM].peak_weight_read_bytes_s; inert on the HBM machine.

rom.interleave_bytes.justification: ROM address stripe, set equal to the burst quantum so consecutive bursts land on consecutive arrays; inert on the HBM machine.

rom.transaction_bytes.justification: ROM burst quantum, set equal to rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array so the model's ceil(transaction_bytes / bytes_per_cycle) is exactly 1 and no bandwidth is lost to quantisation; inert on the HBM machine.

parameters.derivation: 3 sequencer cycles (sequencer.fetch_cycles + decode_cycles + issue_cycles, the cycle model's per-instruction front end) divided by technology.json#latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s = 3e-09 s.  The analytical model states no clock; this is the one analytical quantity that fixes one.  Every rate below is an analytical B/s or ops/s divided by this clock, so a different clock would move the per-cycle numbers and leave every derived TIME unchanged.

The analytical model prices no engine byte-port bandwidth.  Both machines are given the larger of the pair's weight-path rates (4.752960e+14 B/s) so that no simulated time is attributed to an engine port the analytical model does not model.  At the shipped 64 B/cycle this would throttle DMA to 6.400e+10 B/s, 7426x below the ROM array it drains.

technology.json#latency.pipeline_fill_drain_s 3.2e-08 s + one global wire traversal sqrt(reticle.area_mm2) x global_wire_delay_s_per_mm = 4.282231e-09 s, the analytical array-pass boundary 3.628223e-08 s, times the clock = 36.2822 cycles.  The analytical model charges 4 of these per layer; the cycle model charges one per engine instruction and has no per-layer hook, so the difference between the deployment's instructions per layer and 4 is a reported residual, not a tuned parameter.

The narrowest tensor operator output width in Qwen3-8B (1024: the GQA key and value projections, num_key_value_heads x head_dim).  At batch 1 the cycle model's tensor rate is min(lanes, tile_cols*issue_window, cols) x work_per_lane_cycle x clock, so lanes above the operator's own output width are masked and deliver nothing.  1024 is the largest lane count for which EVERY tensor operator of this model runs at the full derived roof; at 4096 the achieved rate falls to 88.5% of the roof and at 12288 to 42.6%.  The pair (lanes, work_per_lane_cycle) is a gauge split of one analytical quantity -- their product times the clock is what the design point pins -- and this rule fixes the split by exactness.

compute roof / (lanes x clock), in work-counter units.  The roof is area_fractions.compute 0.22290895663237373 x silicon_area_mm2 3260.0 x technology_derivations.compute_ops_s_per_mm2.bf16 679903147699.7579 x efficiencies.compute 0.55 = 2.7174080677e+14 ops/s.  Verified against the artifact: 15136811008 ops / that roof = 5.570312088214652e-05 s, which reproduces the published component_times_s.compute 5.570312088214652e-05 EXACTLY, to the last bit in double precision.  Units: the cost table declares this parameter in work/lane/cycle and the shipped characterized value was measured as (tensor.multiplications + tensor.additions) / cycles; the analytical operations count is multiplies AND adds too (operations_per_active_parameter = 2), so no conversion is needed and none is applied.  That makes the machine's MAC rate lanes x work_per_lane_cycle / 2 x clock = 1.3587040338e+14 MAC/s.  In the cycle model this value divides the K extent (ceil(tile_depth x work_scale / work_per_lane_cycle)), so it is the reduction-tree width of one output lane -- 132.69 MACs deep -- and not a second lane count.

One HBM3E channel.  points[ROM] serves KV from 20 stacks at 1.800000e+13 B/s and points[GPU] serves weights and KV from 16 stacks at 1.440000e+13 B/s; at 8 channels per stack both give 112.5 B/cycle at this clock.  The two design points buy different numbers of the SAME channel, which is why hbm.channels is the only HBM parameter the two machines are permitted to differ on.

20 HBM3E stacks x 8 channels.  points[ROM].area_fractions.hbm_phy 0.06134969325153374 of 815 mm2 per device at 10 mm2 per stack over 4 devices, serving KV alone at 1.800000e+13 B/s (kv_transfer_bytes_per_step / component_times_s.kv_read).
Set equal to the HBM burst so consecutive bursts stripe across channels.

The analytical layer_fixed_latency charges one KV round trip per layer: sram_access_s 2e-09 + one global traversal 4.282231e-09 = 6.282231e-09 s = 6.2822 cycles.  KV lives in HBM on both sides of this anchor, so that primitive is the HBM access latency.

16 independently-addressable ROM arrays, the ROM bank count the shipped Qwen ROM deployment plans (capability memory.rom.banks; the ROM lowering stripes one bank per weight role). points[ROM].peak_weight_read_bytes_s 4.7530207238e+14 B/s (= rom area 1746.5168 mm2 x technology_derivations.rom_read_bytes_s_per_mm2 x efficiencies.rom_read_bandwidth, already derated) divided by 16 arrays and by the clock = 29706.379523, rounded to 29706.  Achieved aggregate 4.7529600000e+14 B/s, -0.00128% against the analytical value.
Set equal to the ROM burst so consecutive bursts of one weight object land on consecutive arrays and a sweep engages every array.

The analytical model prices no ROM access latency.  The ROM array is on die, so the one analytical latency primitive that applies is a global wire traversal of the reticle: sqrt(reticle.area_mm2 815.0) x global_wire_delay_s_per_mm 1.5e-10 = 4.282231e-09 s = 4.2822 cycles.

Set equal to rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array so that the cycle model's max(1, ceil(transaction_bytes / bytes_per_cycle)) is exactly 1 and the array delivers its full derived rate.  The analytical model has no burst-size concept, so this is the only constraint on the value.

The cycle model builds NO fabric on TopologyClass.SINGLE_CHIP (runtime/cycle/fabric.py:923-930), so a single-chip run has structurally zero link cycles.  Both anchor points are multi-device tensor-parallel machines charging 72 nvlink5 all-reduces per token.  The derived machines express each anchor as ONE logical device holding the aggregate resource of its design point, which is exactly the transformation that removes the inter-device fabric; the term is therefore absent by construction and is reported, not approximated.  Both sides pay almost the same link tax, so removing it does not favour either machine -- it inflates the ratio, and the published ratio is recovered by adding the two analytical link terms back.

The five analytical component times do NOT sum to the analytical step.  step = max(memory_time, compute_time) / efficiencies.stage_balance x token_slots + link_latency + layer_fixed_latency, with memory_time = weight + kv when the design point shares one memory path (the GPU point) and max(weight, kv) when it does not (the ROM point).  Both anchor points have token_slots = 1 and pipeline_stages = 1, so the only extra factor is stage_balance = 0.9, applied because devices > 1.  Collapsing each point to one logical device sets devices = 1, so the derived machines do not carry it either; it is worth 1.11x on both sides and is reported.

The two models do not agree on the total arithmetic.  The analytical count for this model is the explicit active-parameter fallback, active_parameters 7568405504 x 2, with NO attention arithmetic and no context dependence.  The cycle model counts attention separately (attention.score_multiplications, attention.value_multiplications), which at context 8192 is 2.416e+09 extra MACs per token.  The models agree on the weight-driven multiply count and disagree on the total; this is structural and cannot be tuned away.

The analytical ROM weight_read term is a full sweep of the STORED array: stored_weight_bytes 16381470720 / peak_weight_read_bytes_s = 3.446539e-05 s, identical for every batched ROM design in the study.  The cycle model has no full-sweep semantics: it charges only the bytes the deployment's accesses touch, and at batch 1 the weight amplification is 1, so it will charge engaged_weight_bytes 15136811008 (92.40% of stored).  The reconciliation must compare the cycle model's ROM traffic against the engaged bytes and report the sweep-versus-touched difference as a modelling divergence, not a machine parameter.

The analytical term is 1.894112e-07 s per layer built from four primitives; only the array-pass boundary has a cycle-model counterpart, and the cycle model charges it per engine INSTRUCTION, not per layer.  The layer barrier (3.5e-08 s per layer, 1.260 us per token) has no counterpart on a single chip at all.
